text:
julia: quick question about /v1/generate responses — should we always return Content-Type: application/json even when the body is a plain string in the structured-output field? also what's our recommended pattern for optional fields: omit vs null?

max: prefer application/json for anything JSON-shaped. avoids content sniffing. if we ever stream, use text/event-stream or application/ndjson for SSE.

sam: about omit vs null: my take — omit for optional fields that are not relevant; use null only when the field existed previously and you want to explicitly clear it (ie semantic difference). but that makes client schema stricter.

tanya: +1. Also: we should version the response contract somehow so clients can detect compatibility. thinking header like `X-Redwood-Response-Schema: v2` or `Content-Schema: application/vnd.redwood+json; version=2`?

kevin: header sounds good. adding a header is non-breaking for the wire. FYI streaming complicates headers (canary vs fallback) but doable.

julia: here's a tiny example of what I mean — current schema (v1) vs proposed v2 snippet:

```json
v1 example:
{
  "id": "abc123",
  "text": "Hello",
  "metadata": {"lang":"en"}
}
\nv2 idea (structured output optional):
{
  "id": "abc123",
  "output": {
    "text": "Hello",
    "blocks": [{"type":"paragraph","text":"Hello"}]
  },
  "metadata": null
}
```

julia: question — should `metadata` be dropped entirely (omit) in v2 or set to null for explicitness?

max: if we keep omit as default we can avoid changing payload size. but clients doing `response.metadata?.foo` might break if they expect object. recommend docs: optional objects are optional (may be omitted). add example code in SDK: `const meta = response.metadata ?? {}`.

sam: for schema validation on the server side, I suggest we validate strict shape for `output` and allow unknown fields at top-level for forward-compat. server should emit a deprecation warning (log/metric) if old fields like `text` are present alongside `output`.

tanya: +1 on metrics. I'll add a small alert to detect clients that fail with missing metadata. Also we should add a migration note for enterprise private deploys — they might be pinning v1 schema.

kevin: can we do a canary rollout: add header `X-Redwood-Response-Schema: v2` for 10% of traffic and keep v1 by default? deploy-bot can tag the release.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for endpoint /v1/generate with response-schema v2 header — rollout 10% -> 50% pending · job: deploy/2026-03-17-09

julia: thanks — action items: (1) docs PR with header + SDK guidance (julia) (2) server schema validation + metric for old-field usage (sam) (3) canary rollout config + deploy plan (kevin/tanya). I'll open PRs and ping reviewers.

max: small nit on nullable: if a field is allowed null in schema, explicitly document when null vs omitted. otherwise client devs get confused.

julia: will do. pinging @kevin for review once I open the PRs.

kevin: I'll review. also add a short e2e test that verifies both `metadata` omitted and `metadata: null` paths.

sam: PR link when ready?

julia: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-inference/pull/4521 (docs + schema header) — draft.

kevin: looking. :eyes:

tanya: tagging product-API so they know about the header change. cc @product-api

julia: ok thanks everyone. keeping this thread for coordination — will update with PR numbers and canary metrics. :thumbsup:
